run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T12:11:01Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is explained by a fault on the shipping→quote hop. Frontend error spans exist only on the checkout path (POST /api/checkout and its children), and the same one-to-one error propagates through checkout (oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, HTTP POST) and shipping (/get-quote and its client span POST quote). During 12:11–12:19 every failing shipping→quote call ran longer than 10,000 ms (a ~10s client timeout) while successful ones stayed fast, and quote's own POST /getquote server spans in the same window were all ≤100 ms with no errors — i.e. the timed-out calls never reached quote's application. Baseline 12:00–12:08 shows 258 shipping→quote calls all ≤200 ms, so this is a step change, not saturation. Coincident with the error window, 63 Chaos-Mesh events from source component podnetworkchaos were emitted for exactly three pods — shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 and both quote pods (quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b, quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt) — from 12:09:03Z to 12:19:03Z, matching the observed onset and clearing of errors. All 22 otel-demo pods were Running/Ready with zero restarts, so pod failure/OOM is not the cause. Entities with their own failure evidence: frontend, checkout, shipping and frontend-proxy. Quote showed no failures of its own (fast, error-free spans and continued successful processing) and its inbound span volume fell from 259.2 to 44.2 per 8 minutes; it is the target of the network chaos, not an application failure.

claims.text: Frontend error spans in 12:11:02–12:27:02 are confined to the checkout path: POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, POST and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder each increased by 240.11 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, while its other operations (GET /api/products/{productId} 2361.8, POST /api/cart 843.59, GET /api/cart 428.17, GET /api/data 470.67, GET /api/recommendations 451.54) had 0 error spans.

In the same 16-minute window, nonzero ERROR-status increases existed only for frontend (the four checkout-path operations, 240.11 each), checkout (oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 240.11, HTTP POST 240.11), shipping (/get-quote 240.11, POST quote 240.11), frontend-proxy (ingress 243.30, router frontend egress 242.24) and flagd EventStream spans in ad (1.06) and recommendation (1.06); cart POST and flagd ResolveBoolean, payment GET/dns.lookup/tcp.connect/flagd, and accounting 'orders receive' were returned with 0.

Over the whole authorized window (increase over 76m ending 12:27:02) the only nonzero ERROR increases are frontend checkout-path operations 283.65 each, checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 266.82 and HTTP POST 266.82, shipping /get-quote 266.82 and POST quote 266.82, frontend-proxy ingress 298.82 and router frontend egress 285.61, plus flagd EventStream spans in recommendation 4.06, ad 2.04 and fraud-detection 2.04.

Onset: frontend error spans are 0 in every 2-minute bucket from 11:57 through the point at 12:09:00 and jump to 167.25 at 12:11:00 (bucket covering 12:09–12:11); shipping's first nonzero 2m bucket is 12:12:00 with 69.33 error spans.

Course of the burst in 4-minute buckets: frontend 127.15 at 12:11:01, then 292.11–404.99 through 12:21:01, and 0 at 12:23:01 (that series' data ends at 12:23:01); checkout and shipping follow the same shape (147.89–204.85 per bucket, 0 at 12:23:01), while payment and cart stay 0 throughout.

shipping's client span POST quote during 12:11–12:19: 214.59 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans and 44.21 non-error spans; every error span is above the 10,000 ms bucket (le=10000 = 214.59 = +Inf, le=5000 = 0), while non-error spans are ≤5000 ms (18.33 ≤10 ms, 23.72 ≤100 ms).

Baseline for the same client span, 12:00–12:08: 258.13 POST quote spans of which 250.67 were ≤100 ms and 258.13 ≤200 ms (none above 200 ms), a comparable baseline that the incident window departs from.

quote's own server span POST /getquote during 12:11–12:19 is 44.21 spans, all ≤100 ms (43.13 ≤10 ms) and none above 100 ms; its 12:00–12:08 baseline is 259.2 spans, 258.13 ≤10 ms and all ≤100 ms. Quote therefore served no slow request in either window, so the ~215 shipping calls that hung did not reach quote's application.

quote's span statuses in the 16m window: POST /getquote, calculate-quote and {closure} each returned 51 spans, all STATUS_CODE_UNSET; no quote ERROR series appears in the cluster-wide ERROR inventory (it returned only UNSET series for quote).

Checkout's other dependencies were not slow during the same 12:11–12:19 window: oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 44.21 calls and oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert 512.22 calls, all ≤100 ms (payment 32.35 ≤10 ms); checkout's returned ERROR series exist only for HTTP POST and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (266.82 each over 76m) while CartService/GetCart, CurrencyService/Convert, PaymentService/Charge, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart appear only with STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

Chaos-Mesh events: 63 events with source component podnetworkchaos, reason Updated, type Normal, message 'Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource', involving exactly three pods — quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b, quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt and shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 — with timestamps 12:09:03Z through 12:19:03Z at roughly 55–60 s intervals.

All 22 pods in namespace otel-demo were Running, ready=true with restartCount 0 and start times 2026-11-15T11:34:51Z–11:36:51Z; quote runs 2 replicas (quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b on node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e, quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt on node i-0f88eaa39b314c60b) and shipping 1 replica (shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 on i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e).

Service endpoints were populated: the quote Service lists both quote pods (100.96.4.53 and 100.96.2.155) and the shipping Service lists shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 (100.96.4.227); the checkout and frontend Services each list their single pod.

Both quote pods kept logging successful work during the error burst: quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b logged 'Calculated quote' repeatedly between 12:07:42Z and 12:19:00Z (including 12:11:02Z, 12:11:58Z, 12:12:58Z, 12:16:58Z, 12:17:58Z, 12:19:00Z) and quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt logged it through 12:19:02Z; the returned lines contain only that message.

In the shipping log slice covering 12:18:34Z–12:19:31Z there are 40 'Requesting quote' lines but only 5 'Sending Quote' and 5 'Tracking ID Created' lines, i.e. shipping started far more quote requests than it completed.

Ownership chain and resources: shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 is owned by ReplicaSet shipping-75d58f5d84 and both quote pods by ReplicaSet quote-6b5877698d; images are ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-shipping and ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-quote; container limits are cpu 5m/memory 15Mi (shipping) and cpu 5m/memory 40Mi (quote), identical to the baseline period.

The flagd-config ConfigMap's demo.flagd.json at query time has defaultVariant 'off' for all twelve feature flags (including paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, adFailure).

Most likely cause: a Chaos-Mesh network fault applied to shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 and both quote pods from ~12:09 to ~12:19 stalled shipping's HTTP POST calls to quote until its ~10 s client timeout (all failing calls >10,000 ms, while quote saw only fast successful requests). That failed shipping's /get-quote server span, then checkout's PlaceOrder and HTTP POST, and produced the frontend POST /api/checkout 5xx error spans that the RequestErrorRate alert reports.

Rejected: quote application hang or CPU starvation (its container CPU limit is 5m). If quote were hanging, its own POST /getquote spans would show long durations, but every quote span in 12:11–12:19 was ≤100 ms (43.13 of 44.21 ≤10 ms), it logged successful 'Calculated quote' lines throughout, and the identical 5m CPU limit handled 259.2 requests in the 12:00–12:08 baseline with all spans under 100 ms.

Rejected: general node or cluster-wide network degradation. In the same incident window checkout's calls to PaymentService/Charge (44.21) and CurrencyService/Convert (512.22) were all ≤100 ms, and the pods sharing the affected nodes (including flagd, frontend, payment, cart, product-catalog and all other workloads) were Running/Ready with zero restarts.

Rejected: a flagd feature-flag fault (e.g. paymentFailure/productCatalogFailure/cartFailure) as the cause. All flags read 'off' at query time, no ERROR series exist for payment, cart or product-catalog request paths in the 76m window, and the flagd-related ERROR spans that do appear (recommendation 4.06, ad 2.04, fraud-detection 2.04 EventStream spans over 76m) are on long-lived flagd event streams in services outside the failing checkout→shipping→quote hop.

Rejected: pod crash, OOM or eviction. All 22 otel-demo pods (including both quote replicas and shipping) were Running with ready=true and restartCount 0, all started ~11:34–11:36Z, and the only events present for the window are the 63 podnetworkchaos updates — no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Unhealthy entries were returned.

quote is not itself failing: both replicas are registered Service endpoints, both served error-free sub-100 ms requests during the burst, and its span statuses are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no ERROR series). Its observable change is a drop in inbound work (259.2 → 44.21 POST /getquote spans per 8 minutes), consistent with requests not arriving rather than with quote returning errors.

gaps: Jaeger trace data was stale: the newest spans returned were from 11:55:04Z–11:55:07Z, before the 12:09–12:20 error burst, and traces_search_by_tags with error=true / otel.status_code=ERROR / http.status_code=500 returned no traces in the windows tried. The per-span error messages and status codes of the failing shipping→quote calls are therefore unknown.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule was not found in Prometheus (rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data), so the metric and expression behind the reported 'current: 1.111111111111111' and its denominator are unverified; only the trace-span error signals could be checked.

The Chaos-Mesh NetworkChaos/PodNetworkChaos objects themselves (and their fault type, loss/delay parameters, direction and duration) are not readable through the permitted kinds; only the chaos controller's per-pod 'Updated' events are visible, so the exact injected fault characteristics are unverified.

Kubernetes events were retained only for 12:09:03Z–12:19:03Z; any earlier or later chaos activity, rollout or probe events are unknown, and absence of other event types in the returned list is not proof that nothing else happened.

Container logs were only readable through ~12:19Z (read_through 12:19:00–12:19:31), so application behaviour after 12:19Z is unknown; the error-word filtered log reads for quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b, shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 and checkout-5dccddf8bb-vz2zd returned no lines (status no_data), which does not prove no errors were logged.

kube-state-metrics series (e.g. kube_deployment_status_replicas_available/ready, kube_pod_owner) returned no data in this Prometheus, so deployment-level readiness history could not be checked; pod status and Service endpoints were used instead.
change_history is not an integrated data source for this run, so no deployment/configuration change records could be correlated with the 12:09Z onset.
Kafka, email, accounting and image-provider request paths were not examined beyond their span error series (no error signals observed); their deeper health is unchecked.
next_steps: Inspect the Chaos-Mesh NetworkChaos/PodNetworkChaos resources selecting shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9, quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b and quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt (direction, loss/delay percentage, duration) with a chaos-mesh-aware tool or kubectl to confirm the fault parameters and whether the experiment was deliberate.

Confirm the RequestErrorRate alert's expression and the meaning of its 1.111111111111111 value from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule configuration, since the rule is not present in the queried Prometheus.
Retain or extend Jaeger trace retention for the incident window (or collect the collector's error attributes) to capture per-span error messages/status for the shipping→quote timeouts.
Review shipping's HTTP client timeout (~10 s) and retry behaviour toward quote, since the observed impact is dominated by requests blocking until that timeout.

If the network fault was not intentional, treat shipping↔quote network policy/routing on nodes i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e and i-0f88eaa39b314c60b as the remediation focus; verify after any cleanup that shipping POST quote latency and frontend POST /api/checkout error spans return to the 12:00–12:08 baseline (all shipping→quote calls ≤200 ms, zero error spans).
